lede: The biggest thing on the government calendar this week is Mountain Village Town Council taking up first reading of an ordinance that would move Housing Authority fees out of the municipal code and into an annually updated fee schedule — a structural shift in how affordable housing costs get set going forward. Alongside that, the County Housing Code Update working group meets Tuesday on proposed changes designed to remove Land Use Code barriers to workforce housing, HARC takes a hard look at a potential demolition of Rebekah Hall — the Town-owned building where HARC itself meets — and the BOCC has a full plate including a view-plain MOU tied to a 1999 settlement.

notable.stake: Policy decision on subpar bedrooms in mitigation units affects real housing supply.
County working group shapes Land Use Code changes to unlock workforce housing production.
HARC reviews potential demolition of Town-owned Rebekah Hall, a historic landmark.
BOCC takes up view-plain MOU and constitutional amendment discussions with regional impact.
Two public hearings on subdivision and PUD applications — public comment accepted.
First reading: ordinance shifts MVHA fee-setting out of municipal code, changing housing cost structure.
